explanations.2: This line makes the script exit immediately if any command fails, treat undefined variables as errors, and handle pipes correctly—it's a safety net for scripts.
explanations.23: The syntax ${1:-.todos} means 'use the first argument if provided, otherwise default to .todos'—it's a concise way to set a fallback value.
explanations.24: Same pattern as line 23: use the second argument if given, otherwise default to 4.
explanations.28: The -printf '%f\n' option prints just the filename (not the full path) of each file found.
explanations.29: This sed command strips everything at the start of the filename up to the first digit, then captures the first run of digits that is at least 3 digits long—it extracts the ID number regardless of status prefixes like DONE_ or PARTIAL-.
explanations.34: The 10# prefix forces bash to treat the number as base-10 instead of octal, so a number like 020 is read as twenty, not sixteen.
explanations.35: The ${width} syntax inserts the width variable into the printf format string, so if width is 4, it becomes %04d (pad with zeros to 4 digits total).
